newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil-Firm on tight supplies in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil-Firm on tight supplies in thin trade.

text.p: The Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market firmed on Monday amid tight supplies in quiet trading as sellers were sidelined in the absence of fresh arbitrage exports from the Middle East, traders said.

They said supplies were also tightened by the shutdown of Shell Singapore's 11,000 tonne per day (82,000 barrel per day) thermal gas oil complex which produces mainly fuel oil, in addition to gas oil and kerosene.
The unit was shut down on Saturday for a 21-day scheduled maintenance, a company spokeswoman said.
Supplies in Singapore is already tight due to the absence of incremental spot exports from the Middle East where demand is strong.
Traders said the 380-cst market is especially tight due to improved bunker demand with the 180/380 cst spread narrowing to about $2.50 per tonne in both the bunker and cargo market.
Bunker sales on Monday topped 20,000 tonnes with prices edging up by about $1.00-2.00 per tonne, they said.
The firmer sentiment was reflected in the swaps market where September paper traded at $101.75 per tonne, up about 50 cents from Friday.

Traders said part of state-owned Petroleum Authority of Thailand's (PTT) purchase of 80,000 tonnes for August delivery was covered from the U.S. with some of the September-delivery cargo also expected to be covered from there.

PTT awarded its tender to buy 72,000 tonnes of September delivery 2.0-percent 180-cst fuel oil to Japanese trader Petrodiamond at a $8.05-per-tonne premium to Singapore spot quotes on a cost-and-freight basis, industry sources said.
